attribution.note: These are Marcus's own words in his own Substack post. They are not a quote of the embedded tweets.

semantics.note: The draft keeps the 'seems' hedge on Huang's support ('appears to have supported'). The first clause, that China wanted the chips, is categorical, but the claim's substance is the hedged clause about Huang.

contract.note: The contract is fair: it sets no support or contradiction condition because the Huang clause is hedged. Treating both clauses as one claim, rather than scoring the categorical first clause alone, is an evaluator choice, and it is reasonable.

reviews.rationale: Marcus hedges the main assertion with 'seems', saying only that Huang appears to have supported China getting Nvidia chips. Under policy, hedged statements are not scored. The packet has no evidence items, and the contract rightly sets no grading conditions. So the outcome is not_adjudicable.
